children: Peru on Tuesday cut its 2026 economic growth outlook to 3.1% from a previous estimate of 3.4%, citing adverse effects on some of the country's key production sectors due to the El Niño weather phenomenon.
The government maintained its projection for economic growth next year at 3.4%.

The ministry also said it now expects a wider fiscal deficit next year, projecting it will climb to 2.0% of GDP from a  previous estimate of 1.4%. For this year, it cut its 2026 fiscal deficit projection to 1.2% from 1.8%

The ministry said El Niño "is expected to affect production in primary sectors, particularly fishing, agriculture, and primary manufacturing," and warned that "inflationary pressures associated with high international oil prices" may also impact growth
Warming ocean temperatures brought about by El Niño are upsetting Peru's Pacific ecosystems, putting its fishing sector and over a million people in vulnerable areas at risk, scientists have said
The weather pattern is also threatening fishmeal and fruit exports, which have been major growth drivers in recent years
Peru's Coast Guard on Tuesday temporarily closed 58 of the country's ports and partially shuttered 47 others as a result of strong swells caused by El Niño
